description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. The platform supports traceability, information exchange and risk management in the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) area. The contract will also support interoperability with local systems and relevant international platforms, as well as gradual alignment with the EU IMSOC approach, including TRACES NT, RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS-related functionalities, where relevant.

title: Small Arms Range Construction Pease ANGB
description: This notice constitutes an Invitation for Bids (IFB), Solicitation W50S8A-27-B-A002 for the construction of a Small Arms Range at Pease Air National Guard Base (ANGB) in Newington, NH. The Government seeks to award a single firm fixed price contract for services, non-person, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools equipment, appliances and supervisors needed to for the demolition of an existing range on that site and the construction of a new range facility according to the plans, designs, drawings, and specifications. The anticipated contract duration shall be 455 days after the notice to proceed. Please refer to the attached SF1442 for a complete listing of applicable provisions and clauses. Also note that the Government is setting this requirement aside as a total 100% small business set aside under NAICS 236220 which has a small business size standard of $45.0M. The associated PSC is Y1JZ.Interested parties shall provide their bids to the Government by the closing and time of this solicitation and shall be available for public opening at the time and date specified in Block 13 of the SF1442. Bids shall be either submitted electronically via the solicitation module in PIEE or hand carried to the Portsmouth Armory on opening day. The Government will not accept bid submission by any other means. Interested bidders are strongly encouraged to review the instructions to Bidders in section 00 21 00 of the solicitation. This posting also constitutes a notice of pre-bid conference and site visit which the Government will conduct on December 10, 2026 at 10:00 AM (EST) on-site at Pease ANGB in Newington, NH. Please see paragraph 4 of section 00 21 00 for details regarding site access. Interested parties shall note that there exists a brand-specific aspect to this requirement. Specifically, the newly constructed range must have Monaco fire-alarm components. See the attached brand name justification for full details. In accordance with FAR 36.211(b), the following information is provided: (1) The National Guard has no agency-specific policies or procedures applicable to definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts other than those described at FAR 43.204, DFARS 243.204 and AFARS 5143.204.(2) Data for the prior 3 fiscal years regarding the time required to definitize equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts for the National Guard is currently not available but will be compiled and provided in future announcements.

title: Kiinteistöjen ulkoalueiden hoito: Alueurakat
description: Hankinnan kohteena on tilaajan hoitovastuulla olevien kohteiden ulkoalueiden ympärivuotinen tai kausittainen hoito aluekohtaisesti. Palveluun sisältyvät tarjouspyynnön liitteiden mukaiset ehdot (hankinnankuvaus ja sopimusluonnos) ja tehtävät, joita ovat urakkaohjelman, tehtäväkorttien, määräluetteloiden ja karttojen mukaiset talvi- ja kesähoitotehtävät. Tarjoaja vastaa koko palveluketjusta, myös alihankkijoiden työstä, tiedonkulusta ja raportoinnista. Hankinnan osa-alueet: Alueurakat 1. Oulu Keskusta 2. Oulu pohjoinen 3. Oulu etelä 4. Oulunsalo 5. Haukipudas Tarkempi hankinnankuvaus liitteenä. Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhtä tai useampaa osa-aluetta. Jokainen osa-alue vertaillaan ja palveluntuottaja valitaan voittavan hinatvertailun perusteella. Hankinnan perusteella tehdään jokaisesta osa-alueesta erillinen palveluhankintasopimus. Hinnat ilmoitetaan arvonlisäverottomina euroina. Hintoihin sisältyvät kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta aiheutuvat kustannukset, kuten työ, työnjohto, kalusto, polttoaineet, matkakorvaukset, matkat, päivärahat, varallaolo, raportointi, vakuutukset, hallinto ja tavanomaiset tarvikkeet. Laskutus-, toimitus- tai toimistokuluja ei hyväksytä. Kunkin osa-alueen vertailuhinta muodostuu "hankinnan kohteen kriteerit" kohdassa ilmoitetuista aluekokonaishinnoista ja erillisyksikköhinnoista sekä Oulunsalon ja Haukiputaan osalta myös kiinteiden hintojen osalta (auraus ja hiekoitus). Liitteenä ovat osa-aluekohtaiset tarjouslomakkeet (excel), joiden avulla saadaan aluekokonaishinta. Tämä hinta syötetään cloudiaan kohtaan "hankinnan kohteen kriteerit" ja siellä syötetään myös kysytyt erillisyksikköhinnat. Tavoiteltu sopimusmalli on 1 vuoden määräaikainen sopimus ajalla 01.10.2027 - 30.09.2028, jota voidaan jatkaa tilaajan päätöksellä yhden vuoden optiokaudella 01.10.2028 - 30.09.2029. Tämä ajanjakso koskee osa-aluetta 1 ja 4, keskusta, Oulunsalo. Osa-alueella 2, 3 ja 5 (Oulu pohjoinen, Oulu etelä ja Haukipudas) sopimusmalli on 1 vuoden määräaikainen sopimus ajalla 01.06.2027 - 30.09.2028, jota voidaan jatkaa tilaajan päätöksellä yhden vuoden optiokaudella 01.10.2028 - 30.09.2029. Tämän jälkeen kaikki sopimukset jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana alkaen 01.10.2029- 30.9.2031, jos osapuolet niin kirjallisesti sopivat ennen optiokauden kauden päättymistä. Sopimusehdot JYSE2025 mukaisesti. Sopimusluonnos liitteenä., Alueurakka 1 Oulu keskusta Oulun keskusta-alueen alueurakka. title: Tienvarsiteknologian kapasiteettilaitteistot ohjelmistoineen
description: Tienvarsiteknologian kapasiteettilaitteistot ohjelmistoineen Hankinnan kohteena ovat Fintraffic Tie Oy:n (jäljempänä myös "Hankintayksikkö" ja "Tilaaja") nykyisen tienvarsiteknologian kapasiteettipalvelun (jäljempänä myös "TVT-KaPa") korvaava kapasiteettilaitteistot tarvittavine ohjelmistoineen. Hankinnan kohde ja sen vaatimukset on määritelty tarkemmin tarjouspyyntöaineistossa. Toimituksen tavoitteena on rakentaa Tilaajalle uusi, tuotantokelpoinen, turvallinen, vikasietoinen ja hallitusti ylläpidettävä konesaliympäristö sekä siirtää sovitut nykyiset palvelut ja työkuormat uuteen ympäristöön. Toimituksen lopputuloksena Tilaajalla tulee olla käyttövalmis konesali- ja virtualisointiympäristö, keskitetysti hallittava verkko- ja tietoturvaratkaisu, hallittu virtuaalikoneiden ajopalvelu, hallittu kontti- ja Kubernetes-palvelu, hallittu tietokantapalvelu, hallittu kuormantasauspalvelu, hallittu varmistus- ja palautumisratkaisu, keskitetty valvonta ja lokitus, automatisoitava ja versionhallittu konfiguraationhallinta sekä dokumentoidut ylläpito-, muutos-, häiriö- ja palautumismenettelyt. Toimittaja vastaa siitä, että toimitetut osakokonaisuudet muodostavat yhteentoimivan kokonaisuuden ja ovat valmiita tuotantokäyttöön. Hankittavien laitteiden ja ohjelmistojen lisäksi hankintaan kuuluu tarvittavat käyttöönotto- ja migraatiopalvelut, korjaus-, asennus-, asiantuntija- ja jatkokehityspalvelut sekä ohjelmistopäivitykset (tarvittaessa) ja VMware Virtual Cloud Foundation 9 (VCF9) -teknologian myötä tulleiden uusien ominaisuuksien lanseeraamisen nykyisestä alustasta hankittavaan ratkaisuun. Hankittavien laitteiden tulee sisältää viiden (5) vuoden 24/7 ylläpito laitteistojen toimittajan taholta. Tilaaja hankkii kapasiteettilaitteistot liikenteenhallinnan työkuormien ajoon. Hankinnalla tavoitellaan maksimaalista käytettävyysastetta, selkeää ja toimintavarmaa arkkitehtuuria perus- ja poikkeustilanteissa. Ratkaisun tulee perustua Hyperkonvergenssilaitteisiin (jäljempänä HCI), VMware-virtuaalikoneiden virtualisaatioalustapalveluun (VSAN ready klusteri) ja varmistusratkaisuun sekä NAS-levyjärjestelmään. Nykyinen kapasiteettiratkaisu perustuu VMware vSphere virtualisointiteknologiaan, erillisellä NAS levyjärjestelmällä ja tallennusratkaisulla. Kapasiteettialustan virtualisointiteknologia päivittyy hankinnan myötä hyödyntämään VMware Virtual Cloud Foundation 9 teknologiaa. Tilaaja jatkaa VMware teknologian käyttöä ja on erikseen hankkinut tarvittavat lisenssit VMware alustalle. TVT-KaPa:n automatisoidusta valvonnasta, operoinnista ja vikatilanteisiin liittyvästä työnohjauksesta vastaa Tilaajan hallinta- ja valvontapalveluja toimittava, ns. ”HALVAL-toimittaja”. Lisäksi HALVAL-toimittaja vastaa jo olemassa olevista fyysisistä konesaliverkoista sekä Tilaajan runkoverkosta. Hankintayksikkö valitsee kilpailutuksen perusteella kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimman tarjouksen tehneen tarjoajan, jolta tilaukset tehdään. Kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimpana pidetään tarjousta, joka on hinnaltaan halvin. Hankittaville palveluille asetetut laadulliset vaatimukset ja näkökulmat on otettu huomioon vähimmäisvaatimuksissa. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin. LISÄHANKINTAMAHDOLLISUUDET (OPTIO) VARMUUSKOPIOINTILAITTEISTO Hankintaan sisältyy optiona kapasiteettilaitteiston varmuuskopiointilaitteisto (backup) ohjelmistoineen. Varmuuskopiointilaitteiston vaatimusmäärittely on hankintailmoituksen julkaisuhetkellä vielä kesken, mutta aikataulullisista syistä Hankintayksikkö ei voi enää lykätä kilpailutusta. Vaatimusmäärittelyä ei ole mahdollista tehdä loppuun ennen hankintailmoituksen julkaisua. Varmuuskopiointilaitteiston vaatimusmäärittely tullaan tekemään sopimuskauden aikana. Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden optiona hankkia varmuuskopiointilaitteiston sopimustoimittajaksi valitulta tarjoajalta. Hankintayksikkö ei kuitenkaan ole velvollinen hankkimaan laitteistoa sopimustoimittajalta, vaan Hankintayksikkö voi harkintansa mukaan hankkia varmuuskopiointilaitteiston myös muulla tavalla, esimerkiksi kilpailuttamalla. Optiona hankittavan varmuuskopiointilaitteiston arvo voi olla enintään 500 000 euroa (alv 0 %). MUUT LISÄHANKINTAMAHDOLLISUUDET Hankintaan sisältyy optiona laitejärjestelmien muutos- ja laajennusmahdollisuudet, jotka on kuvattu liitteessä B.4 Hinnat. Lisäksi Hankintayksikkö voi hankkia tarpeen vaatiessa sopimuskauden aikana muita sellaisia laitteita ja ohjelmistoja, jotka se kokee tarpeelliseksi esimerkiksi jatkokehityksen kannalta, ja jotka eivät muodosta merkittävää osaa sopimuksen arvosta. Optioiden mahdollinen käyttöönotto on hankintayksikön oikeus, ei velvollisuus.,

Netherlands – Detection and analysis apparatus – Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) Radio Frequency (RF) Equipment
description: The Contract involves the acquisition of IV&V RF Equipment, including Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), for the Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) unit of the RNLASF. The RNLASF operates a fleet of rotary and fixed-wing aircraft. The aircrafts are equipped with Radio Frequency (RF) self-protection equipment. The EW unit supports functioning of this equipment. In view of operational deployment, it is important for the EW unit to know the performance of its hardware and software to enhance its capabilities. The to be acquired IV&V RF Equipment will provide the EW unit better insight into performance of the RF self-protection equipment. To maintain the safety during operational deployment of the aircraft of the RNLASF, the EW unit has to continue to enhance the performance of the RF self-protection. To be able to do this, new IV&V RF Equipment is required as the current equipment is outdated. This Contract mainly contains delivery of an Integrated IV&V RF Equipment, consisting of the following products: one (1) Radio Frequency Signal Generator, two (2) Oscilloscopes, two (2) Signal Analyzers and two (2) Vector Network Analyzers. Additionally, ILS will be needed.

buyer: NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board
title: Pre Front Door Integrated Urgent Care Services
description:
NHS Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (CW ICB) are seeking expressions of interest from suitably qualified and experienced providers for the provision of a comprehensive Pre-Front Door Integrated Urgent Care (IUC) model across Coventry and Warwickshire.

This model requires a single, accountable Lead Provider in each of the two geographical areas:
Coventry (Lot 1) and
Warwickshire (Lot 2)

The appointed Lead Providers will be responsible for the end-to-end design, mobilisation, delivery, clinical governance and continuous improvement of a whole-system urgent care pathway spanning NHS 111 interfaces, GP out of hours, UTC/MIU, ambulance conveyance alternatives, Emergency Department front-door streaming, same-day emergency care, diagnostics, community response and neighbourhood urgent care pathways.

The ICB is not seeking a provider of isolated urgent care components. It is seeking an organisation with the scale, capability, and system leadership to deliver an integrated Lead Provider model. Providers must therefore bring together all interdependent services, healthcare professionals and current Providers, including urgent primary care, community response, and mental health crisis interfaces, into a coherent, accountable and high-performing model.

Contract Length is expected to be 5 years, commencing 1st September 2027 with the Commissioner having the option to extend the Contract for up to a further 5 years.

Further details are provided in VI.3

title: MSG Cook Services Lisbon - Portugal
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States of America in Lisbon, Portugal will launch the solicitation on the beta.SAM.gov website. The Embassy of the United States of America in Lisbon, Portugal, intends to issue a solicitation for cooking/food services for the Marine Security Guards. Brief Summary of Work - The Contractor shall provide cooking services for seven (7) Marine Security Guards (MSG). Contractor shall schedule cooking and serving requirements to ensure that these are done in the order and time frame specified and they are to be performed daily, Monday-Friday. Breakfast (from 7:00-9:30am), Lunch (11:00am to 1:30pm) and Dinner (4:30-7:30pm). The Contractor must clean the kitchen, all dishes and appliances after each meal and cause minimal disruption to the normal operation of the facility. The COR (Contracting Officer Representative) shall determine the schedules presented which will meet the needs of the individual facility. All services are to be delivered for 7 of USG Marine security personnel in providing 7 (seven) meals (2 breakfast options, 2 lunch options and 3 dinner options) at the MSGR for U.S. Embassy Lisbon. Groceries: All groceries and ingredients shall be purchased by MSG within a prescribed budget. Contractor shall coordinate with MSG for required items. The anticipated performance period is for a 6 months base year, with one-year option period, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the lowest priced technically acceptable offeror who is a responsible contractor. The Government may award the contract based on the initial offer without discussion. The resultant contract will be a firm fixed price type contract. The Government is planning to hold a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be announced in the solicitation. All contractors have to be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to contract award pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. Interested parties should contact: Embassy of the United States of America Attn: GSO/Procurement Email: LisbonProcure@state.gov Tel: +351 21 770 2507

ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The Government is contemplating an IDIQ with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) CLINs. REQUIREMENTS INFORMATION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), Commander, Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC), Patuxent River, Maryland intends to procure supplies and services for the analysis and evaluation of the existing weight handling systems, including the building structure to which these are attached, their associated hangers, runway rails, pneumatic/electric traveling hoists, and control systems. Contractors may be required to procure, replace, upgrade, and repair all components previously mentioned pertaining to the weight handling system including but not limited to monorails, bridge cranes, jib cranes and gantry cranes of different capacities. The Offeror shall meet all requirements at FAR 52.240-93 Basic Safeguarding of Covered Information Systems. Offerors that are capable of meeting this requirement and can maintain this capability throughout the duration of the effort being solicited, are encouraged to respond. SUBMITTAL INFORMATION (CAPABILITIES STATEMENT) All submissions shall include the Sources Sought Notice name/number, Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size, and Points of Contact (POC), including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. title: Finland – Public road transport services – Lappeenrannan paikallisliikenteen hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Lappeenrannan paikallisliikenteen hankinta tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Yksityiskohtaiset voimassa olevat linjakuvaukset ovat liikennöintisopimusluonnoksen liitteessä 1. Varsinainen sopimuskausi on 01.7.2028 - 30.06.2035 ilman erillistä irtisanomista. Sopimuskausi on kuitenkin 1.7.2028-30.6.2038, mikäli Liikennöitsijä tuottaa liikennöinnin sopimuskauden alusta alkaen vähintään kuudella (6) XL-tyypin ajoneuvolla. Muilta osin liikenteessä käytettävän kaluston ja kaluston määrän tulee täyttää tämän sopimuksen vähimmäisvaatimukset. Tilaaja varaa itselleen mahdollisuuden jatkaa sopimusta enintään kolmella (3) yhden (1) vuoden mittaisella optiokaudella (1 + 1 + 1). Optiokausien käyttämisestä tehdään erilliset päätökset ja niistä ilmoitetaan liikennöitsijälle viimeistään 6 kuukautta ennen varsinaisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Mahdollisessa jatkosopimuksessa noudatetaan tämän tarjouskilpailun asiakirjoissa määritettyjä ehtoja. Sopimuksen osapuolilta edellytetään avointa yhteistyötä, luottamusta ja vuorovaikutusta sopimuksen toimivuuden kehittämiseksi. Liikennöitsijä vastaa siitä, että tarjoamansa palvelu noudattaa lainsäädäntöä ja viranomaismääräyksiä sekä täyttää tässä tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä määritellyt yksilöidyt vaatimukset. Hankinnan kohteena olevassa liikennöinnissä on käytettävä vaihtoehtoisia polttoaineita, siten kuten ne ovat Euroopan parlamentin ja neuvoston asetuksen (EU) 2023/1804 2 artiklan 4 alakohdassa määritelty. Esimerkiksi biokaasu, uusiutuva diesel, sähkö tai vety. Yksityiskohtaiset kalustovaatimukset ovat määriteltyinä liikennöintisopimusluonnoksen liitteessä 4. Liikenteen hoitamiseen suurin samanaikaisesti tarvittava linja-autojen määrä tarjouskilpailun hetkellä liikennöintivuorokauden aikana on 18 linja-autoa. Sopimuskauden aikana liikenteeseen voi tulla Tilaajan tekemiä muutoksia. Muutoksien osuus vuotuisesta liikenteestä voi olla enintään 50 % lisäystä tai 20 % vähennystä sopimuksen vuotuisesta arvosta tarjouspyynnössä esitetystä. Muutosprosentteihin ei lasketa mukaan tämän sopimuksen mukaisia indeksimuutoksia. Muutos voi koskea linjakilometrien, linjatuntien tai autopäivien määrää. Hankinnasta on pidetty markkinavuoropuhelu 24.8.2026, josta on ilmoitettu Hilma-kanavassa. Lisäksi markkinavuoropuheluun ilmoittautuneille on annettu mahdollisuus osallistua kahdenkeskisiin keskusteluihin ja saada tarjouspyyntömateriaalit lausuttavaksi ennen tarjouspyynnön julkaisua. Lappeenrannan seudun joukkoliikenne pyytää tarjouksia tarjouspyynnön liitteenä oleville suoritteille ja aikataulukaavioille, jotka eivät vastaa tarjouspyynnön aikana voimassa olevia aikatauluja ja autokiertoja.

REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. title: VA - SOURCES SOUGHT: Radiation Dosimetry Supplies and Services
description: RADIATION DOSIMETRY SUPPLIES AND SERVICES The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office 20 (NCO 20), is conducting market research on behalf of the Western States Network Consortium (WSNC) to identify potential contractors capable of providing respiratory fit testing equipment to VA medical facilities and clinics. The WSNC is comprised of Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN�s) 17, 19, 20, 21, and 22. VISN 17: Texas, Eastern New Mexico, and Northwest Oklahoma. VISN 19: Montana, Wyoming, Eastern Idaho, Eastern Nevada, Utah and Colorado. VISN 20: Oregon, Washington, Idaho and Alaska. VISN 21: Northern California, Nevada, Hawaii Islands, Philippines Islands, Guam and American Samoa. VISN 22: Southern California, Arizona, New Mexico, Southern Colorado NOTE: Due to anticipated VA reorganization under RISE (Restructure for Impact and Sustainability Effort), VHA facilities covered under this agreement may be adjusted to align with a new organizational structure. The government reserves the right to expand coverage to additional states, including those in VISN 4 (HSA 4.1, 4.2 and 4.3) and VISN 5 (HSA 5.1-5.5). These additions will be processed via contract modification and will not require a separate solicitation, provided that the work remains consistent with the nature and scope of services described herein. Offerors should price their proposals with the expectation that geographic expansion may occur, and the submitted pricing structures will serve as the basis for any added locations. To be considered a responsive and potential source, interested parties shall provide a capabilities statement containing the following information: Business name, address, point of contact, phone number and email address. Business size designation, type, and SAM Unique Identifier Number Affirmation that the vendor is capable of performing in accordance with the attached Requirements Description. Affirmation that the vendor is capable of performing in compliance with the Non-Manufacturer Rule (NMR). List of additional supplies related to this equipment that it can sell. Confirmation whether trade-in credits are available for existing government-owned equipment. Affirmation that it can provide the required annual calibrations of the equipment. Vendors must be able to provide service for a significant portion of the catchment area detailed in the Locations List. The vendor shall identify which locations they can service with their existing capabilities. Additionally, contractors can provide feedback on the attached Radiation Dosimetry Supplies and Services Requirements Description, which may be considered if a solicitation is posted. Provide the requested information to Robin Wilson at robin.wilson3@va.gov before 10:00 AM PST on December 14th, 2026. All questions must be submitted via email, no telephonic inquiries will be accepted. This is a sources-sought notice only. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of verified sources to include qualified SDVOSB/VOSB to perform this potential requirement. Responses received will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. The Government may or may not issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. There is no solicitation available at this time, and this is not a request for quotes. See attached Radiation Dosimetry Supplies and Services Requirements Description

title: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for (3) dredging projects. The areas of consideration for these dredging services are: Calcasieu Bar River Channel, Pascagoula Harbor, and Panama City Harbor. Calcasieu River Bar Channel: Work for the Calcasieu River Bar Channel will require one fully crewed and equipped self-propelled trailing suction type hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -45ft MLLW and place dredged material into the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Sites (ODMDS).Pascagoula Harbor: Work for the Pascagoula Harbor maintenance dredging will require a hopper dredge. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -46 ft MLLW and place dredged material in the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS). Dredged material shall be placed within Pascagoula ODMDS. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within 3-5 miles of the dredge cut. Panama City Harbor: Work for the Panama City Harbor maintenance dredging will require a medium to small hopper. The dredge must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -40 ft MLLW and place dredged material within channel adjacent to the entrance jetty. Dredged material shall be placed within the channel adjacent to the jetty. The transport distance to the designated placement area varies depending on dredge assignment but typically is within one mile of the dredge cut. The Contractor shall commence dredging no later than 30 January 2027 in Calcasieu River Bar Channel. The order of work is as follows: (1) Calcasieu River Bar Channel, (2) Pascagoula Harbor, (3) Panama City Harbor. This solicitation is unrestricted. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 23 October 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $37,000,000.00. Offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to be eligible to receive an award from any Government solicitation. Call 1-866-606-8220 for more information or visit the SAM website at www.sam.gov. After completing SAM, in order to download documents contractors and their subcontractors must register at www.sam.gov. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number. Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. It is the Offerors responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. For additional information or assistance, please contact Cori Caimi, Contract Specialist, email cori.a.caimi@usace.army.mil or Rosalind Shoemaker, Contracting Officer, phone (910) 251-4436, email rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

title: Gate Valve Frame Replacement
description: The purpose of this requirement is to replace two (2) rusted vertical frame pieces and one (1) horizontal brace of the original gate valve assembly. Work requires temporarily removing an existing electric motor-driven actuator and retained top headrail, unbolting the frame from its primary lower concrete headwall connection, field-drilling bolt holes to align and secure the retained headrail to the new vertical components, and reattaching the reassembled structure to the concrete headwall strictly in accordance with original gate manufacturer specifications. Following reinstallation of the headrail and motor actuator, the Contractor shall verify that the gate valve is fully operational, traveling freely and without obstruction between the fully open position and achieving a proper seal upon complete closure. The contractor shall provide all logistics, labor, tools, and the lawful disposal of all materials and removed components IAW Attachment 1, Statement of Work, Dated 01 Sep 2026.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 14 December 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

description: This is a request for information (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS. This request is not a solicitation (Request for Proposal or Request for Quotations) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the government to form a binding contract. The purpose of this request for information is in support of market research being conducted by the Air Force Metrology Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) to identify potential sources and gather information on current capabilities within the market. This synopsis is for planning purposes only and is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party's expense. The level of security clearance and amount of foreign participation in this requirement has not been determined. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked PROPRIETARY will be handled accordingly. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations. Proprietary information or trade secrets should be clearly identified. If, after reviewing these documents, you desire to participate in the market research, you should provide documentation that supports your company's capability in meeting these requirements. Failure to provide documentation may result in the government being unable to adequately assess your capabilities. If you lack sufficient experience in a particular area, please provide details explaining how you would overcome the lack of experience/capabilities in order to perform that portion of the requirement (i.e., teaming, subcontracting, etc.) Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint ventures or teaming arrangements are encouraged. Currently there are no funds available for this acquisition. The United States Air Force (AFLCMC/AFMETCAL) is seeking sources to procure and deliver modernized, fully compatible accessories to support legacy Keysight N5242A Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs). The scope of this effort encompasses the delivery of plug-and-play replacement accessories and physical standards to numerous designated Precision Measurement Equipment Laboratories (PMELs) across the Air Force enterprise. Prospective contractors must demonstrate the technical capability to supply highly specialized, high-precision radio frequency (RF) and microwave calibration accessories that integrate seamlessly with the existing N5242A VNA platform without requiring software modifications or degrading established metrological accuracy. Interested vendors should submit a brief capability statement including company information (DUNS, CAGE, business size), relevant experience, and rough order of magnitude pricing. The NAICS code assigned to this acquisition is 334515 with a size standard of 750 employees. The total estimated quantity is 1 unit over 1 year. Reconditioned, remanufactured, or used material is not acceptable for this item. Offerors responding to this sources sought market research notice must: (1) state whether you are a small or large business, if you are the manufacturer or provide the name of the manufacturer and size info of product you would be offering and the socioeconomic status and indicate small disadvantaged or woman-owned business, veteran owned, service disabled veteran owned, 8(a) historically black college or university or minority institution (HBCU/MI), or a historically underutilized business zone (HUBZone) (2) provide sales history including recent sales to commercial companies (3) advise if your product is a commercial item or if it will be modified; if not commercial at this time, will you be offering this item to the general public in the future. (4) advise if you have the item on a GSA schedule or other Government contract include front page of schedule and the page showing the part is on award (5) provide information concerning the technical capabilities of the product you are interested in offering, including commercial literature/brochures and warranty. Describe any awards you have been involved in that are the same as or similar to what is described in this RFI. Include any other pertinent information which would enable the government to assess your firm�s capabilities (6) advise if you accept the Government purchase card (7) Provide Point of Contact including: company/ institute name, address, phone number and email address (8) provide assigned Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code (9) Verify if your company/institute is listed in the System for Award Management (SAM) (10) State if your company is domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate the country of ownership) (11) Advise how much time you would need to submit a technical proposal if a solicitation is issued (12) provide an estimated price for one each, an estimated price for the total quantity and provide any price quantity discounts based on the total estimated quantity (13) include estimated delivery time for shipment. Ensure only .pdf, .doc or .xls documents are attached to your email. Submit all responses to the listed point of contact. If an email response is not possible, submit by FAX to 937-713-5841 or mail to 813 Irving-wick Dr W., Horton Building, Heath OH 43056-1199. Reference 27E-646A-RF in all correspondence. Responses are due by 12/14/2026 at 2:00pm ET or 1400 hours; however, early responses are encouraged. title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: *Updated 11/20/2026 to include RFI questions and responses* 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. The quoted price MUST be for the REPAIRof the item(s). E. Must adhere to IUID requirements of DFARS 252.211-7003 F. The ultimate awardee of the proposed contract action must be an authorized repair source. Award of the proposed contract action will not be delayed while an unauthorized source seeks to obtain authorization. G. The Government is requesting a Repair Turnaround Time (RTAT) of: 77 days after receipt of asset. Repair Turnaround Time (RTAT) definition: The resultant contractual delivery requirement is measured from asset Return to the date of asset acceptance under the terms of the contract. For purposes of this section, Return is defined as physical receipt of the F-condition asset at the contractor's facility as reflected in the Action Date entry in the Commercial Asset Visibility (CAV) system. In accordance with the CAV Statement of Work, the contractor is required to accurately report all transactions by the end of the fifth regular business day after receipt and the Action Date entered in CAV must be dated to reflect the actual date of physical receipt. The Contractor must obtain final inspection and acceptance by the Government for all assets within the RTATs established in this contract. Please note freight is handled by Navy CAV or Proxy CAV as stated in NAVSUPWSSFA24 or NAVSUPWSSFA25. Throughput Constraint: Contractor must provide a throughput Constraint for eachNSN(s). Total assets to be repaired monthly after initial delivery commences: _____/month (contractor is to fill in #). A throughput of "0" (zero) per monthreflects no throughput constraint. Induction Expiration Date: 365 days after contract award date. Any asset received after this date in days is not authorized for repair without bi-lateral agreement between the Contractor and NAVSUP WSS Contracting Officer. H. IMPORTANT NOTE: Reconciliation Price Reduction: Any asset(s) for which the contractor does not meet the required RTAT will incur a price reduction per unit/per month the contractor is late.
